subject: Realtime model traffic surge — coordinated steps & contractual mitigation
messages:
From: Ben Jensen <ben.jensen@clearpath.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime degradation — spike starting ~08:50 PT

Aisha —

We started seeing 5xxs and elevated tail latency on our real-time endpoint around 08:50 PT. Latency climbs from ~120ms to >1.5s for a subset of requests, and a few calls returned 503s. We routed a small portion of traffic to our warm standby and that reduced errors, but the problem looks broader (affecting two shards).

Attached is a short sample of logs from this morning (801-traffic-sample.log) and a quick heap snapshot we took. The customer impact is production for us — multiple user-facing features rely on the realtime endpoint. Can you confirm if this is related to any capacity changes on your side (autoscaler backoff / eviction events)? We need an ETA on stabilization and what remedial steps Redwood will take.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Jensen
Head of Platform Engineering | ClearPath AI

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: Ben Jensen <ben.jensen@clearpath.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karl_ops@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime degradation — spike starting ~08:50 PT

Ben —

Thanks for the heads-up and for sending the logs. We're actively investigating. Immediate notes:

- I see a burst in token throughput from ClearPath that aligns with your 08:50 window; preliminary signals point to an autoscaler backoff plus increased queueing on two dedicated GPU nodes.
- Short-term (now): we can route a percentage of your traffic to an alternate model variant (lower memory profile) to reduce evictions. This will slightly change latency characteristics; we can toggle per-route.
- Medium-term (1-4 hours): Ops will attempt a controlled buffer drain and temporary capacity reallocation from an adjacent pool. We may need to evict low-priority workloads to free capacity.
- We'll provide a detailed timeline and a mitigation plan PDF shortly.

I have looped in Marissa for contract/credits and Karthik for spike root-cause. We commit to keeping you updated every 30 minutes until stabilization. Proposed immediate actions:

1) Allow Redwood to route up to 25% of traffic to the fallback variant (please confirm).
2) Approve temporary operation-level evictions for non-critical workloads for up to 3 hours.

If you approve, we will start the routing change now.

On it —
Aisha Rahman
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: ClearPath AI surge — quick coordination + credit estimate request

Team —

Summary: ClearPath saw a traffic surge at ~08:50 PT that triggered autoscaler backoff on two GPU nodes in their dedicated pool, resulting in intermittent 503s and high tail latency. We're executing emergency mitigation (fallback variant routing + buffer drain).

Immediate asks:
- Karthik: can you confirm whether the autoscaler backoff was triggered by sustained memory pressure or a transient kernel OOM? Any telemetry we should collect now?
- Jonas: ops will need to perform controlled evictions of low-priority tenants in the adjacent pool. Estimate how long to restore headroom if we drain two nodes (best-case 18 min, conservative 45 min).
- Marissa: go/no-go on offer: proactive goodwill credit up to 10% monthly ARR applied to next invoice, pending engineering postmortem. If legal needs different language, flag it — want to get approval to offer immediately to reduce churn risk.

Attached are the logs Ben sent and the capacity snapshot. I'm drafting a customer-facing mitigation plan (customer_mitigation_plan_v2.pdf) and will attach after edits. I'll keep customer updates to concise bullets and a time-bound credit offer if we need to escalate.

Quick excerpt from the node telemetry (sanitized):
> [2027-07-19T08:49:52Z] node-7 - queue_depth=238, mem_util=92%, eviction_count=3
> [2027-07-19T08:50:05Z] node-7 - autoscaler: backoff=true, next_scale_attempt=2027-07-19T08:57:05Z
> [2027-07-19T08:50:18Z] node-9 - queue_depth=201, mem_util=89%, eviction_count=1

I'll capture everything in the post-incident timeline afterward. Priority is stabilization + a clear customer offer.

Thanks,
Aisha

Ben / Claire —

Short status update: Redwood routed 20% of your traffic to the lower-memory model variant and performed a controlled buffer drain on the two affected nodes. Ops reports headroom recovery at 12:03 PT; we saw errors drop to baseline shortly after. Karthik will deliver a technical RCA and timeline for permanent mitigations.

Commercial gesture: as discussed internally, Redwood is prepared to issue a one-time credit equal to 7% of this month’s usage invoice for ClearPath AI while we complete the post-incident review and hardening plan. If that is acceptable, I will prepare the paperwork and route for approval.

Next steps (owners):
- Karthik: technical RCA and remediation plan (ETA 48 hours).
- Aisha: 30/60/90 day mitigation playbook + monitoring thresholds (ETA 24 hours).
- Marissa (me): draft credit paperwork and follow-up call scheduling (I can get approvals within 48 hours if needed).

Would you be available for a 30-minute sync at 15:00 PT today to review the mitigation plan and closure criteria? If so, I'll send a calendar invite.

Appreciate your patience — we know this is business-impacting and are prioritizing your recovery.

Best,
